services.label: Services
services.heading: What we
services.pricingNote: Your barber tells you the price before the clippers come out. Ring first if you'd rather know beforehand.

items.name: Skin fade
items.note: Zero, double zero or a normal fade. Blended tight, lined up to finish.

items.name: Scissor cut
items.note: All scissors. Shaped to how you actually wear it, styled before you leave.

items.name: Beard trim
items.note: Shaped with the clippers, or lined with the razor and finished with a hot towel.

items.name: Kids' and first cuts
items.note: Under-12s. Patient with the nervous ones, gentle with the first-timers.

items.name: Turkish hot towel shave
items.note: Hot towels, the cutthroat razor and the flame if you want it. Details below.

items.name: Wax
items.note: Nose and ears. Quick and clean, done while you're in the chair.

shave.label: Turkish hot towel shave
shave.heading:
Hot towels.
A cutthroat.
Then the
paragraphs: You choose how far it goes. A straight hot towel shave is as traditional as it gets. Add the razor line-up and the flame, and it's the full Turkish.
Nobody rushes it. Sit back, close your eyes, and let it happen.

quote.text: You can go as traditional as you want or go fully blown Turkish with the razor and flames.
quote.author: Justin Leeming

steps.title: The towels
steps.body: Steaming hot, laid over the face one after another until the skin softens and the beard lifts.

steps.title: The razor
steps.body: A fresh blade in the cutthroat. Slow strokes with the grain, then across it. Lines cut sharp.

steps.title: The flame
steps.body: A lit taper passed over the ears and cheeks. The fine hair goes in a second. Nothing else does.

steps.title: The finish
steps.body: A cold towel to close the skin, balm, a splash of cologne. Out the door looking like you meant it.

families.label: First cuts
families.heading:
Little ones.
First cuts.
paragraphs: Eighteen months old, first time in the chair. Nursery rhymes on, a juice at the end, and a cut that looks smart in the photos. That's how it goes here.
Patient with the nervous ones. Quick with the wrigglers. Dads get done in the next chair while they wait.

quote.text: they were so good with him, playing nursery rhymes for him to help keep him calm and offered a juicy fruit drink for him too
quote.author: Richard J

reviews.intro: Every one of the 60 reviews on Google gives Legend Barbers five stars.

items.author: Richard J
items.text: I used this new barbers for the first time last Wednesday and my skin fade was top class. They also gave my son who is only 18 months his first ever cut and it looks great, really smart and they were so good with him, playing nursery rhymes for him to help keep him calm and offered a juicy fruit drink for him too. Highly recommend.

items.author: Justin Leeming
items.text: I got my haircut on Saturday morning, grade 4 all over. But it wasn't just a grade 4, the level of detail and care Azad took really was first class. You can go as traditional as you want or go fully blown Turkish with the razor and flames. I chickened out but was very pleased with the end results!

items.author: Mr PMU
items.text: Excellent service, didn't have to wait long.

about.heading: A village barbers on

photo.alt: Dyako, owner of Legend Barbers, smiling outside the shop on Main Street, Menston, beneath the sign and the striped barber's pole
photo.caption: Dyako, outside the shop

paragraphs: Dyako runs Legend Barbers on Main Street, Menston. Three chairs in walnut and black, the gold chair by the window, and a price list on the wall. No appointment needed. Walk in and take a seat.

It's the barbers people in the village keep coming back to. Skin fades taken down properly, scissor cuts shaped to how you wear your hair, and the Turkish hot towel shave done the traditional way. Azad is on the chairs too, and the care is the same whoever cuts you.
